extracted_items.content: Those longer continual settings are more realistic and allows us to benchmark more efficiently what a truly lifelong learning agent should be.

In Tab. 8 we report the class ordering of ADE20K that we used for all the reported experiments, following the previous benchmarks [4, 15]. Considering the 100-50, 100-10, and 100-5 settings, reported in the main paper, we note that 44 of the new classes are “things”, while the other 6 are “stuff”. While there is no difference between “things” and “stuff” in semantic segmentation, it is especially relevant in the panoptic segmentation task, where the goal is to separate in different segments multiple instances of the “things” classes, since it introduces additional challenges.
